newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds fail to get carried away pre-wages.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds fail to get carried away pre-wages.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were reasonably steady ahead of today's key wages data, but failed to get carried away by a sharp rebound in U.S. Treasuries after strong U.S. GDP.
*Q1 AWOTE seen up 0.8 percent for an annual 4.3 percent.
Australian bond yields were reasonably steady ahead of today's key wages data, but failed to get too carried away by a sharp rebound in U.S. Treasuries in the face of a strong U.S. GDP.

A 5.6 percent jump in annual GDP in the first quarter sent the U.S. market reeling initially, but a closer look showed a sharper than expected rise in inventories, suggesting that the second quarter growth would be slower, analysts said.
Hopes were also pinned on Washington being close to a balanced budget agreement.
However, while the local market tracked the volatile movements in the U.S., the advance lacked conviction.

"The flow-on effects to Australia are unclear as local markets will be watching the results of average weekly earnings and building approvals figures today and March retail tomorrow," said ANZ Financial Markets in their morning briefing.

Median forecasts for average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) are for a quarterly rise 0.8 percent for an annual rate of 4.3 percent, up from 3.9 percent in the previous quarter, but below the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent tolerance level.

A weaker than expected outcome could stir speculation of a further easing in monetary policy when the RBA board convenes next week, taking into account stubbornly high unemployment, low inflation and the recent patchiness of the economic recovery.

March building approvals are due at the same time, and are forecast to rise 2.0 percent, although estimates range from a 5.0 percent fall to a 15 percent rise, and an outcome at the top end of the range could unnerve the market.

The local short end continued to underperform against the bloc, but could rebound if today's data proves weak. Canadian bonds outperformed the U.S. again at the long end amid hopes that the Federal Reserve will hold policy steady at this month's FOMC, while New Zealand debt consolidated its recent rally.
The 10-year bond contract needs to crack 92.210/92.230 resistance to overcome the market's current sluggishness and take out last week's brief 92.250 peak. The contract bounced from 92.060 in SYCOM.
